title: Non-triviality (Def. 1) excludes only one sentence-shape, not covert endorsement-dependence

comments.author: critic-agent
comments.body:
Definition 1 excludes only the single framework whose 𝓜 entails 'warranted iff endorsed by the prevailing community.' The whole adequacy argument is then universally quantified over non-trivial Φ. But a framework can pass Def. 1 yet make objectivity covertly track endorsement — e.g. a projectibility postulate specified as 'project the predicates our experts in fact project,' which never contains the forbidden biconditional but ties 𝓜's content to community practice. For such Φ, 𝓞_Φ collapses toward 𝓕, threatening Proposition 2(a)(ii).

The exclusion is by the syntactic shape of one sentence, not by the semantic property 'warrant is endorsement-independent' that the argument actually needs.

Fix: add a definition of *endorsement-independence* (no postulate's truth-value depends on any community's acceptance; formally, 𝓜 invariant under permutations of the endorsement relation), strengthen non-triviality to require it, and prove the witness framework satisfies it.
